article:
JAKARTA, investor.id - PT Bhineka Inovasi 

 Ketahanan Energi Tbk (BIKE) menyampaikan pemberitahuan bahwa perseroan resmi mengakuisisi 72% saham PT Berau Usaha Mandiri (BUM) melalui PT Prambanan Nusantara Energi (PNE), anak usaha perseroan.

Direktur BIKE Muhamad Kuswandi menjelaskan, PT Berau Usaha Mandiri (BUM) memiliki area tambang sekitar 500 hektare di Tanjung Redeb, Berau, Kalimantan Timur. Dari area yang telah dieksplorasi sekitar 400 hektare, tercatat cadangan terbukti sekitar 22 juta metrik ton batu bara.

"Manajemen menargetkan produksi sekitar 1,5-2,5 juta metrik ton per tahun. Akuisisi ini disebut menjadi bagian dari strategi transformasi dan diversifikasi usaha BIKE di sektor energi," paparnya dalam keterangan resmi, Jumat (9/10/2026).

 

 Perseroan akan menyampaikan informasi lebih lanjut kepada pihak-pihak terkait sesuai dengan perkembangan proyek dan berdasarkan ketentuan keterbukaan informasi serta peraturan perundang-undangan yang berlaku bagi Perseroan sebagai perusahaan tercatat.

Saham BIKE saat berita ini disusun ada di Rp 2.000 dan sudah terbang 124% dalam sebulan terakhir.

title: Dony Oskaria: Danantara Masih Pertimbangkan Keputusan Masuk BEI
article:
JAKARTA, investor.id – Badan Pengelola Investasi Daya Anagata Nusantara (Danantara) masih mempertimbangkan kemungkinan menjadi salah satu pemegang saham PT Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) melalui proses demutualisasi. Kendati demikian, keputusan investasi tersebut akan memperhatikan ketentuan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) serta kepentingan penguatan pasar modal nasional.

Kepala Badan Pengaturan Badan Usaha Milik Negara (BUMN) sekaligus Chief Operating Officer (COO) Danantara Dony Oskaria menegaskan bahwa demutualisasi BEI harus dilihat sebagai bagian dari transformasi pasar modal menuju tata kelola yang lebih transparan, kredibel, dan mampu meningkatkan kepercayaan investor.

Menurut Dony, pembenahan pasar modal tidak cukup dilakukan melalui perubahan struktur kepemilikan bursa. Reformasi juga harus mencakup peningkatan porsi saham beredar di publik (free float) dan keterbukaan informasi mengenai pemilik manfaat akhir (ultimate beneficial owner) perusahaan tercatat.

“Ini sedang dipikirkan. Tentu OJK sudah mengeluarkan peraturannya, yaitu 5%. Di atas 5% harus mendapatkan persetujuan,” ujar Dony ketika menjawab pertanyaan peserta dalam Investor Daily Summit (IDS) 2026 di Hotel Raffles, Jakarta, Kamis (8/10/2026).

Dony menjelaskan, kemungkinan Danantara masuk sebagai pemegang saham BEI tetap terbuka. Namun, pihaknya belum mengambil keputusan final mengenai investasi tersebut. “Danantara tentu melihat ini, mungkin juga kita akan masuk. Tetapi kalaupun masuk, itu tentu mengikuti ketentuan daripada OJK,” kata dia.

Lebih jauh, Dony menekankan bahwa demutualisasi BEI merupakan momentum penting untuk memperbaiki tata kelola pasar modal Indonesia. Perubahan struktur kepemilikan diharapkan dapat memperkuat transparansi serta meningkatkan kredibilitas bursa di mata investor domestik maupun internasional.

“Pada intinya, demutualisasi bursa ini adalah bagaimana kita membuat lebih transparan. Ini adalah komitmen kita kepada investor, komitmen negara untuk membuat bursa kita lebih transparan,” tegas dia.

Menurut Dony, reformasi pasar modal juga harus memastikan investor memperoleh informasi yang memadai mengenai perusahaan tempat mereka menanamkan modal. Karena itu, peningkatan free float dan keterbukaan pemilik manfaat akhir menjadi bagian penting dari agenda pembenahan.

“Tidak hanya mengenai ownership daripada bursa yang akan diperbaiki, tetapi juga free float-nya akan dinaikkan. Kemudian, ultimate beneficial owner-nya juga akan dibuka lebih transparan,” ujar dia.

Dengan transparansi yang lebih baik, investor diharapkan dapat mengambil keputusan berdasarkan informasi yang mencerminkan kondisi sebenarnya dari emiten dan pasar modal Indonesia.

Demutualisasi sendiri merupakan perubahan struktur kepemilikan bursa yang sebelumnya melekat pada anggota bursa menjadi struktur yang memungkinkan masuknya pemegang saham dari luar anggota bursa. Perubahan tersebut diharapkan dapat memperluas basis kepemilikan, memperkuat tata kelola, dan mengurangi potensi benturan kepentingan dalam pengelolaan bursa.

Sebelumnya, sebagaimana diberitakan Antara pada 30 September 2026, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Danantara Rosan Roeslani memperkirakan porsi kepemilikan Danantara dalam proses demutualisasi BEI sekitar 5–10%. Adapun kepemilikan melalui konsorsium yang berpotensi melibatkan kementerian atau lembaga pemerintah lainnya dapat mencapai 30–40%. Namun, Rosan menegaskan bahwa pembahasan mengenai komposisi kepemilikan tersebut masih berlangsung.

Sementara itu, OJK telah menerbitkan Peraturan OJK (POJK) Nomor 13 Tahun 2026 tentang Pemegang Saham Bursa Efek. Regulasi tersebut menetapkan batas kepemilikan saham bursa sebesar 5% bagi setiap pemegang saham, dengan kemungkinan pengecualian untuk kepemilikan yang lebih besar setelah memperoleh persetujuan OJK.

Kepala Eksekutif Pengawas Pasar Modal, Keuangan Derivatif, dan Bursa Karbon OJK Hasan Fawzi sebelumnya menjelaskan bahwa kepemilikan di atas 5% harus melalui proses penelaahan dan persetujuan regulator. Dengan demikian, besaran kepemilikan Danantara tidak dapat ditentukan secara sepihak.

Di sisi lain, sebagaimana diberitakan Antara, Danantara telah menyampaikan minat untuk menjadi salah satu pemegang saham Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) melalui skema demutualisasi. Minat tersebut disampaikan melalui Danantara Investment Management (DIM).

Hasan menambahkan, BEI masih menyiapkan perubahan sejumlah peraturan internal dan anggaran dasar untuk melaksanakan demutualisasi. Pasalnya, ketentuan yang berlaku saat ini masih membatasi kepemilikan saham BEI pada anggota bursa. Karena itu, perubahan anggaran dasar harus terlebih dahulu memperoleh persetujuan melalui rapat umum pemegang saham (RUPS).

“RUPS dulu, karena anggaran dasarnya harus diubah. Anggaran dasar tidak boleh diubah tanpa melalui mekanisme RUPS,” kata Hasan di Jakarta, Kamis (8/10/2026).

Dengan demikian, peluang Danantara menjadi pemegang saham BEI masih bergantung pada penyelesaian tahapan demutualisasi, keputusan pemegang saham bursa, dan pemenuhan ketentuan OJK.

title: Haji Isam Masuk, Low Tuck Kwong Jaga Porsi Elaine Low
article:
JAKARTA, investor.id – PT Jhonlin Baratama – perusahaan Haji Isam – resmi menggenggam saham PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN).

Direksi Bayan Resources (BYAN) mengungkapkan bahwa perseroan telah menerima surat-surat pemberitahuan dari Dato’ Low Tuck Kwong dan Elaine Low tertanggal 8 Oktober 2026 yang menyampaikan bahwa transaksi pengalihan 10.084.088.370 saham Bayan kepada Jhonlin Baratama telah diselesaikan pada 7 Oktober 2026.

Dari total tersebut, Low Tuck Kwong mengalihkan 10.067.421.703 saham BYAN dan Elaine Low mengalihkan hanya 16.666.667 saham. Elaine Low merupakan putri dari Low Tuck Kwong. Di sini terkesan, Low Tuck Kwong menjaga porsi kepemilikan anaknya.

Setelah transaksi, Low Tuck Kwong secara langsung menggenggam 3.316.166.832 (9,95%) saham BYAN, sedangkan Elaine Low memiliki 7.350.500.368 (22,05%) saham.

Sebelum transaksi dengan perusahaan Haji Isam, Low Tuck Kwong sempat mengalihkan 33.333.335 saham BYAN kepada Elaine Low di harga Rp 11.025 per saham pada 6 Oktober 2026. Sehingga kepemilikan Elaine Low sempat meningkat dari 22% ke 22,10%.

Kemudian, Elaine Low turut menjual 16.666.667 saham BYAN kepada perusahaan Haji Isam pada 7 Oktober dan karenanya kepemilikan Elaine Low menjadi 22,05%. Porsi Low Tuck Kwong sendiri menyusut drastis dari 40,15% menjadi 9,95%.

“Tidak ada perubahan pengendalian di perseroan,” tegas direksi Bayan Resources dalam keterbukaan informasi dikutip Jumat (9/10/2026).

Adapun berdasarkan laporan dari Low Tuck Kwong dan Elaine Low kepada otoritas bursa, harga transaksi dilakukan di Rp 2.588. Sehingga nilai keseluruhan pelepasan 10.084.088.370 saham Bayan kepada Jhonlin Baratama mencapai Rp 26,09 triliun.

title: MUFG and Danamon propose Bank MUFG Danamon name for integration
Indonesia Targets Rp 1.7 Trillion From Sweetened Drink Tax in 2027
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia plans to collect Rp 1.7 trillion ($102 million) from an excise tax on packaged sugary drinks in 2027, with the levy expected to take effect in the second half of the year as the government seeks to curb consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages amid the country’s growing diabetes burden.

The government is still finalizing implementing regulations, including the tax rate and the sugar-content thresholds that would determine which beverages are subject to the levy, Director General of Customs Djaka Budhi Utama said Friday.

“The 2027 state budget law already stipulates an excise tax on sweetened packaged beverages, with a revenue target of around Rp 1.7 trillion,” Djaka told reporters at the Finance Ministry’s monthly state budget briefing in Jakarta.

“We are still completing the regulations and hope the tax can be implemented in the second half of 2027,” he said.

The proposed levy is intended to cover packaged drinks containing added sugar. Potential products under discussion include carbonated soft drinks, energy drinks, sweetened flavored beverages and other ready-to-drink products.

The public-health challenge is substantial. Indonesia’s Health Ministry estimates that 20.4 million people in the country have diabetes, placing Indonesia fifth globally by the number of people living with the disease.

The Indonesia Health Survey (SKI) 2023 found that diabetes prevalence among people aged over 15 reached 11.7% based on blood-glucose testing. The total number of people with diabetes could reach 30 million, according to estimates cited in the supplied data, while only around 10 million to 15 million have been diagnosed.

Sugary-drink taxes are intended to discourage consumption by raising the price of products with added sugar and potentially encouraging manufacturers to reformulate their beverages. However, the impact of Indonesia’s planned levy will depend partly on its final rate, which products it covers and the sugar thresholds used.

Discussions on the rate are continuing between the Directorate General of Customs and the Finance Ministry’s Directorate General of Economic and Fiscal Strategy, Djaka said. The government has yet to determine the final scope of the tax or how much sugar a beverage must contain to be subject to excise duties.

The government previously proposed an excise rate of Rp 1,500 per liter for ready-to-drink beverages and Rp 2,500 per liter for concentrates, syrups and extracts. Those proposals have not been finalized for implementation in 2027.

The Rp 1.7 trillion revenue target is lower than the Rp 7.6 trillion figure discussed in earlier deliberations, reflecting changes to the plan as the government prepares technical rules and considers industry conditions and consumers’ purchasing power.

The proposed excise is part of wider efforts to regulate the consumption of products high in sugar, salt and fat. Government Regulation No. 28 of 2024 on Health provides a regulatory basis for measures to control the consumption of such products.

The final design of the tax, including its rates and the beverages covered, will depend on the implementing regulations now being prepared.

title: ‘It’s Trump Who Sets Oil Price’: Prabowo’s Brother
article:
Jakarta. President Prabowo Subianto’s brother Hashim Djojohadikusumo recently said global oil prices rest in US leader Donald Trump’s hands, as crude kept climbing above $100 a barrel.

Speaking at the Investor Daily Summit, Hashim — who is also the president’s climate envoy — said that Indonesia had “strong fundamentals” as he once again tried to assuage public pessimism over the economy. He went on to name oil prices as the only obstacle that Jakarta is facing.

“Neither the Indonesian government nor OPEC set the oil price,” Hashim said, referring to the oil cartel of Arab nations.

“It’s President Donald Trump who can do so. If he stops the war with Iran, the oil price will drop.”

Hashim — a seasoned businessman who runs an oil business under his Arsari Group — then told the forum in jest that he would be “kind of sad” when crude prices fall. He added: “But I suppose that’s okay. I can still make money.”

“Let's not be influenced by those social media posts of a 'dark Indonesia'. It's actually bright, even more so once the Hormuz reopens.”

Around a fifth of the world’s oil freely passed through the waterway before the US and Israel launched a surprise attack in Tehran in late February.

Since then, Iran has taken advantage of its geographic location to block passages in retaliation, fueling price hikes across the globe.

The global crude benchmark Brent stays high above the $100 per barrel threshold as the US-Iran talks hit an impasse. Trump had also repeatedly declared the Hormuz as a US “territory”.

Two Indonesian oil tankers were even trapped in the Hormuz Strait for months in the aftermath, although these vessels had made it back home. The disruptions also prompted Indonesia to seek Russian crude as an alternative.

According to Chief Energy Transition Minister Bahlil Lahadalia, Indonesia’s oil demand amounts to 1.6 million barrels per day, but some 1 million barrels come from imports. In addition to beefing up lifting, Indonesia is tapping into its palm oil abundance to produce biodiesel to narrow the gap. The country has even mandated a 50% palm oil-based blend in the diesel sold at its pumps as part of a policy known as B50.

“With B50, I’m confident we can stop importing diesel fuel with the C48 [Cetane 48] specification this year,” Bahlil told the same conference.

title: ‘Follow The Money’: Indonesia Steps Up Illegal Import Crackdown
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia has once again waged war on illegal imports, with one newly appointed senior deputy minister saying that more efforts should be put into examining the money transfers.

The Prabowo Subianto administration wants to curb illegal imports with hopes that it can bring economic growth up to 6% next year and eventually 8% by 2029 or the end of the presidential term. Dradjad Hari Wibowo, the deputy coordinating minister for economic affairs, claimed on Thursday that the government already “found out who was behind the illegal imports”.

“We already know the perpetrators. All that remains is how we can bring imports to order. I have proposed that we should follow the money. Wherever illegality exists, we must follow the money,” Dradjad — who had only spent a week in the cabinet — told the recent Investor Daily Summit in Jakarta.

“We shall have more effective enforcement in the order.”

He did not go into detail on what the government had up its sleeve. Dradjad, who was on Prabowo’s campaign team as an economist, later claimed that he knew the “tricks” to sniff out illegal importers.

“Illegal import has been deeply entrenched here. A ministry official once told me that they could face physical threats when they were about to take measures against them,” Dradjad said, without naming his source.

He admitted to being concerned by the uncontrollable arrivals of used clothing that usually enter the country in bales. Authorities reported that a bulk of the secondhand shirts and dresses enter the country via Malaysia, with the deliveries bound for the domestic thrift market.

Just a few weeks ago, customs authorities seized thousands of bales of used clothing, which were worth at least Rp 8 billion ($447,077).

It was also around that time when Prabowo gathered his ministers to save the textile industry, which employs around 4 million workers and records $12 billion in annual exports, according to a government estimate. This labor-intensive sector has been facing mass layoffs, part of which is due to its inability to compete with cheap imports.

“[The president] has ordered Customs Head [Djaka Budhi Utama] to immediately take care of the bales entering our country. They have really harmed our garment producers,” chief economic minister Airlangga Hartarto said.

title: Rupiah Strengthens to Rp 17,899 per Dollar Despite Fiscal Deficit
article:
Jakarta. Rupiah extended its gains against the US dollar on Friday, strengthening despite Indonesia’s widening budget deficit and continued geopolitical tensions between Washington and Tehran.

The rupiah closed 16 points, or 0.09%, higher at Rp 17,899 per dollar on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, compared with Rp 17,915 in the previous session.

Traze Andalan Futures Director Ibrahim Assuaibi said the rupiah strengthened despite the release of Indonesia’s latest state budget figures, which showed a deficit of Rp 319 trillion, equivalent to 1.24% of gross domestic product (GDP), as of September 2026.

Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara reported that state revenue had increased 25% year-on-year, while government spending rose 19%. Total state revenue reached Rp 2,341.5 trillion, equivalent to 74.2% of the full-year target of Rp 3,153.6 trillion.

Externally, the rupiah gained ground despite ongoing tensions between the United States and Iran.

On Thursday, US President Donald Trump said Washington was holding productive discussions with Tehran and reiterated that there were no plans for an attack before the US congressional midterm elections on Nov. 3, 2026.

On the same day, Iranian news agency Tasnim reported that Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran was reviewing Washington’s response to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.

Meanwhile, developments in US monetary policy remained in focus after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said further interest rate increases were necessary, while maintaining flexibility over the pace of tightening.

Other currencies traded against the rupiah on Friday included the Singapore dollar at Rp 13,982, the Japanese yen at Rp 113.25, the Australian dollar at Rp 12,488 and the euro at Rp 20,078.

title: Indonesian Stocks Gain 1% Despite Global Market Jitters
article:
Jakarta. Indonesian stocks rose 1.04% on Friday as resilient domestic consumer confidence and retail activity helped the market withstand global pressures from geopolitical tensions, fears of an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble and uncertainty over China-European Union trade relations.

Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) gained 62 points to close at 6,093, after moving between 5,995 and 6,100 during the session. Trading volume reached 28.3 billion shares, with turnover totaling Rp 9.9 trillion and transaction frequency exceeding 1.4 million. A total of 381 stocks advanced, 238 declined and 172 remained unchanged.

Pilarmas Investindo Sekuritas said relatively stable domestic economic conditions supported the market despite mounting external pressures. Bank Indonesia’s (BI) September 2026 consumer confidence index stood at 118.1, remaining in optimistic territory.

Meanwhile, the real sales index grew 1.3% year-on-year (yoy), accelerating from 1.1% in July 2026.

“These data show that consumer confidence and domestic sales activity remain resilient. However, purchasing power still needs attention to ensure that positive perceptions of current economic conditions do not diverge from consumers’ expectations for the future,” Pilarmas said in its research note on Friday.

On the global front, investors monitored US President Donald Trump’s remarks that he would not attack Iran before the Nov. 3, 2026, midterm elections.

Trump said talks with Tehran had been productive, although the United States would maintain its naval blockade of Iran and would not allow the country to possess nuclear weapons.

Concerns over OpenAI’s revenue outlook also reignited fears of a bubble in the AI industry, Pilarmas said. Investors have begun questioning the prospects for returns on investments in the sector, putting pressure on US technology stocks.

Markets were also awaiting the outcome of trade talks between China and the European Union in Beijing. The discussions came amid concerns among European industries over Chinese trade practices, the EU’s goods trade deficit and Beijing’s restrictions on exports of critical minerals.

“The combination of these factors weighed on global markets. Major European stock markets and Wall Street fell again, extending pressure on global benchmark indices,” Pilarmas wrote.

In Asia, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 closed nearly unchanged at 69,030.92. The Shanghai Composite Index edged up 0.1%, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index rallied 1.6%. South Korean markets were closed for the day.

title: Indonesia Spends $32 Billion on Education Through September
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia spent Rp 574.2 trillion ($32.07 billion) on education through September 2026, accounting for 21.6% of total state spending of Rp 2,660.5 trillion, Finance Deputy Minister Suahasil Nazara said on Friday.

The education budget funded student assistance, teacher and lecturer salaries and allowances, free nutritious meals for schoolchildren, and the operation and improvement of educational facilities, Suahasil said at the Finance Ministry’s October edition of its APBN KiTa press conference in Jakarta.

The funding supports several government programs, including the Program Indonesia Pintar (PIP), which provides financial assistance to school students; the Kartu Indonesia Pintar Kuliah (KIP Kuliah), which helps students cover the cost of higher education; and the free meal program (MBG).

The allocation also covers salaries and allowances for teachers, lecturers and other education personnel, including both civil servants and non-civil servants. Funding for school operations, higher education institutions and early childhood education centers is provided through various operational assistance programs.

Suahasil said education spending was distributed through multiple channels, including central government expenditure, transfers to regional governments and financing allocations.

“Some funds are disbursed through central government expenditure, some through transfers to regional governments, and some through financing,” he said.

The arrangement allows central and regional governments to combine funding from the state budget (APBN) with locally generated revenue to meet education needs.

“That is why I always say that the APBN and regional budgets (APBD) are one integrated whole,” Suahasil said.

Total state spending reached Rp 2,660.5 trillion as of September, equivalent to 69.2% of the full-year budget allocation. Education spending accounted for approximately 21.58% of the total expenditure realized during the period.

title: Indonesia Braces for MSCI Review in November
article:
Jakarta. November will be a crucial time for the Indonesian capital market as index provider MSCI will release its delayed review.

MSCI has given Indonesia time until November, warning that it could downgrade Jakarta to "frontier" markets from the current "emerging" status if it fails to make sufficient progress. MSCI’s warnings over transparency and coordinated trading had led to reforms at the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX).

As the clock ticks toward MSCI’s review, FTSE Russell recently decided to keep Indonesia unchanged in the secondary emerging market group and away from its watchlist. Financial watchdog OJK’s chief capital market supervisor Hasan Fawzi said that the decision showed that Indonesia’s market reforms were heading in the right direction.

"Hopefully, this will be a benchmark for other index providers and global investors’ attitude towards Indonesia’s commitment to continuously improve its market integrity and investability,” Hasan told Investor Daily Summit in Jakarta on Thursday.

Jakarta hopes for “objective” assessments. However, he said that the ongoing capital market reforms were not solely meant to address MSCI’s concerns, citing that Jakarta had wanted to strengthen its investability.

Iding Pardi, a director at the IDX, told the same conference that the bourse had intensively engaged with global index providers and international investors to show that the reforms had been underway.

“The decisions of the global index providers are out of our control. But what we can make sure of is that our capital market’s transformation is delivering the expected impact,” Iding said.

Iding also told the audience that it’d be unwise to gauge the health of the capital market just by the movement of the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) alone. Such analysis must take into account the listed companies’ fundamentals, trading liquidity, capital raising, and share ownership structure.

The JCI touched an all-time high of 9,135 in January before the steep drops. By mid-year, the market began to show signs of gradual recovery.

title: Indonesia Needs More Than Market Size to Sustain Investment Growth
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia’s strong investment growth will need to be matched by deeper technology adoption, skilled talent and stronger links to global supply chains if the country wants to sustain that momentum.

Indonesia recorded Rp1,010.6 trillion ($56.47 billion) in investment in the first half of 2026, up 7.2% from a year earlier and equivalent to 49.5% of its full-year target, according to the Investment Ministry.

The government is also attracting more capital into downstream industries, with investment in the sector reaching Rp300.1 trillion, or 29.7% of total investment, in the first half, up 6.9% year-on-year.

The figures come as Indonesia seeks to make investment a bigger driver of economic growth by combining its large domestic market and natural resources with foreign capital, technology and access to global markets.

“More importantly, this is not only the size of the market, but the economic growth that we are having,” Deputy for Investment Promotion at the Investment Ministry Nurul Ichwan said at the Investor Daily Summit 2026 in Jakarta on Thursday.

Nurul said Indonesia’s economy has maintained growth of around 5% since the COVID-19 pandemic, while its natural-resource base provides opportunities for investors. For foreign companies, however, Indonesia’s market potential is increasingly tied to whether the country can support more technology-intensive operations and connect them to wider supply chains.

Nugraheni Utami, chief country representative of the US-ASEAN Business Council, said global companies consider how their Indonesian operations fit into their businesses in other countries.

“Because the market itself is not about Indonesia, but how they can expand their operation, and also supporting Indonesia’s purpose to export the products to other countries,” Utami said.

She said Indonesia’s young, tech-savvy workforce was another important investment advantage.

“Also with the young tech savvy population, easy to adapt with the technology. I think that's one of the most important factors for investors coming to Indonesia,” Utami said.

US companies are also contributing to Indonesia’s technology capacity. Utami said USABC members had identified 90 innovations from 43 companies operating in Indonesia and trained more than 1 million people through technology capacity-building programs.

The United States was the fifth-largest source of foreign investment in Indonesia in the first half of 2026, contributing $1.7 billion.

Utami said the recently signed US-Indonesia trade agreement could further support Indonesian-based production by improving access to the US market.

“If Indonesia gets the lower tariff, it creates more investors rethinking their global investment decision to Indonesia as part of the global supply chain,” she said.

title: Government Rules Out Giving Up Control of Bank Jakarta in 2027 IPO
article:
Jakarta. The Jakarta administration plans to retain a controlling stake in Bank Jakarta when the regional lender goes public, with an initial public offering (IPO) targeted for the first half of 2027.

Governor Pramono Anung said on Friday the city government must remain the bank's majority shareholder even as it prepares to sell shares to public investors, emphasizing that government control over the lender is nonnegotiable.

The ownership requirement will be incorporated into a draft regional regulation proposed by the administration to ensure that Bank Jakarta remains under Jakarta's control following its stock market debut.

"There is no room for management or authority to be transferred to any other party. I will not allow that," Pramono said.

He stressed that both Bank Jakarta and the city-owned drinking water company PAM Jaya must remain under the Jakarta administration, underscoring his commitment to maintaining public control over strategically important regional enterprises.

However, the precise ownership structure for Bank Jakarta's planned IPO has yet to be finalized.

"The final decision will be made after this receives approval through the regional regulation. Therefore, we are waiting for the regulation," Pramono said.

The proposed regulation will provide a legal framework for determining the administration's ownership position before the bank proceeds with its public offering.

IPO to Support Capital Expansion

 Bank Jakarta previously announced plans to launch its IPO in the first half of 2027 as part of a broader strategy to strengthen its capital base, improve corporate governance and increase transparency through public market oversight.

The planned listing is also expected to support the bank's ambition to enter the Bank Based on Core Capital (KBMI) 3 category, which covers lenders with core capital of between Rp 14 trillion and Rp 70 trillion ($782.5 million to $3.9 billion).

As of June 2026, Bank Jakarta reported core capital of Rp 10.97 trillion on a standalone basis and Rp 12.59 trillion on a consolidated basis.

Based on the consolidated figure, the bank would need an additional Rp 1.41 trillion in core capital to reach the Rp 14 trillion threshold, assuming no other changes to its capital position.

The planned IPO could provide an opportunity to raise fresh funds while introducing greater market scrutiny of the bank's financial performance and management.

However, the amount of capital raised and the proportion of shares offered to public investors will depend on the final IPO structure, which remains subject to regulatory approval and the Jakarta administration's ownership requirements.

title: Danantara to Follow OJK Rules on IDX Ownership
article:
Jakarta. Danantara said Thursday that it would play by the rules set by the financial watchdog OJK as the fund explores plans to buy a stake at the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX).

Indonesia is in the midst of opening up its bourse to public ownership, a move better known as demutualization. The OJK has rolled out a regulation, requiring its green light for any IDX purchase of more than a 5% stake. Indonesia is still ironing out the details, but Danantara’s top brass have repeatedly floated IDX ownership plans.

“Danantara will take a look at the possibility. But even if the stake purchase does happen, we will certainly follow OJK’s rules on the 5% ownership,” Danantara chief operating officer Dony Oskaria told the recent Investor Daily Summit in Jakarta.

He went on to say that Danantara is still deliberating on the decision.

“A [demutualized exchange model] is part of Indonesia’s commitment to boost its transparency.”

IDX is pursuing demutualization following index providers’ scrutiny, which had caused stocks to tumble. Other reforms include a minimum free float hike from 7.5 to 15%, on top of publication of information on shareholders owning over 1% of listed companies.

In its recently published regulation, OJK has capped the IDX ownership at 5%. But anyone who exceeds the limit must gain the watchdog’s approval as long as it brings “added value” to the bourse, such as strong capital and technological capabilities.

State news agency Antara, quoting OJK’s chief capital market supervisor Hasan Fawzi, recently wrote that IDX was still working on the changes to existing rules amid Danantara’s interest. The speed of the demutualization completion also hinges on the exchange’s readiness.

Danantara boss Rosan Roeslani had signaled that the fund’s stake would be within the 5% to 10% range.

title: Indonesia Rewrites Its Economic Model to Power Faster Growth
article:
Jakarta. Indonesia wants to grow faster without remaining dependent on the commodities that have long powered its economy.

Southeast Asia’s largest economy is betting that investment, mineral value-added processing, and a sweeping overhaul of state-owned companies can propel economic growth toward 8%, while renewable energy and digital infrastructure create new engines beyond commodities.

That was the broad message from the two-day Investor Daily Summit 2026 in Jakarta, held under the theme “Indonesia’s Economic Model.” Senior officials described an economic strategy that gives the state a large role in directing capital, industrial policy and the restructuring of state-owned companies, while seeking greater participation from private investors.

Rosan Roeslani, investment and downstream industry minister and chairman of Danantara, Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund and state-asset manager, offered the government’s shorthand for the strategy.

“Downstream industry is the engine of transformation, while investment is the engine of growth,” he said.

The government is targeting more than Rp13,000 trillion ($780 billion) of investment over the next five years to support its 8% growth ambition. Investment rose from Rp1,714 trillion in 2024 to Rp1,931 trillion in 2025 and reached Rp1,010.6 trillion in the first half of 2026, creating about 1.45 million direct jobs, Rosan said.

From Ore to Industrial Chains

 Raw-mineral processing, or hilirisasi in Indonesian, sits at the center of Indonesia’s economic model. Rather than exporting raw materials, the government wants its mineral wealth to feed domestic manufacturing, capturing more value and creating jobs along the way.

Nickel is the showcase. Indonesia has developed an increasingly integrated ecosystem covering ore, anodes and cathodes, battery cells, packs, and recycling. Nickel exports rose roughly tenfold, from about $3.3 billion in 2016-17 to around $33 billion in 2025, as more processing moved onshore, Rosan said.

The harder task is completing the chain. Bahlil Lahadalia, the newly appointed coordinating minister for downstream industry and energy transition, has warned against turning Indonesia into merely a supplier of semi-finished goods that are exported and eventually return as finished products.

That means pushing deeper into manufacturing, rather than stopping at smelters and intermediate products.

Dony Oskaria, Danantara’s chief operating officer, said the state-asset manager is itself part of this transformation. It is mapping companies by industry, benchmarking their performance globally and consolidating a sprawling state-enterprise network.

Danantara aims to reduce roughly 1,074 state-linked entities to about 250, eliminating duplication and improving the use of state assets. It is also assessing companies in finance, infrastructure, and mining that could be listed from 2027, using capital markets to impose greater transparency and accountability.

“We need to become an industry-based country. That is why the government is pushing to accelerate industrial development, particularly industries that can create a large number of jobs,” Dony said. He added that Danantara had already undertaken 21 downstream projects.

Energy is the Constraint

 Industrialization has an inconvenient arithmetic: factories, mines, and data centers all require electricity. The energy transition is therefore becoming an economic question, not merely an environmental one.

Bahlil said Indonesia is developing a 100-gigawatt-peak solar program requiring about $73 billion of investment. Once completed, it could reduce the government’s electricity subsidy and compensation burden by roughly Rp 70 trillion.

The government also plans to raise ethanol blending, beginning with E20 in 2027-28 and eventually reaching E50, in an effort to curb gasoline imports. It is even exploring electricity exports, although Bahlil said energy deals must protect national interests.

Geopolitics makes the calculation harder. Wars and rivalries far beyond Indonesia are disrupting supply chains and threatening to raise fuel costs.

“Geopolitics is not merely a tension between the United States, Israel, Palestine, Ukraine, and Russia. Almost everyone is affected, including Indonesia,” Bahlil said.

Beyond Mines and Factories

 Indonesia’s next growth cycle cannot depend entirely on heavy industry. Hashim Djojohadikusumo, President Prabowo Subianto’s special envoy for climate and energy, pointed to housing, construction, and the digital economy as additional sources of demand.

Housing and construction are linked to about 185 industries and account for roughly 14% of GDP, he said. Meanwhile, affordable internet, artificial intelligence, and data centers could open another frontier — provided Indonesia can produce enough electricity to power them.

“Indonesia has a competitive advantage in the era of AI and data centers,” Hashim, President Prabowo Subianto’s younger brother, said.

The government has announced a 100GW solar program equipped with energy-storage batteries, he added.

title: Indonesia Enters New EV Industry Era with First Battery Exports
article:
Central Halmahera. Indonesia marked a new milestone in its ambition to become a major player in the global electric vehicle (EV) supply chain on Thursday, as President Prabowo Subianto launched the country's first EV battery exports and 11 industrial projects worth $10.2 billion at the Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP) in North Maluku.

Seven of the 11 projects are entering the construction phase, while four have begun commercial operations, according to Investment Minister Rosan Roeslani.

The industrial projects cover nickel-based battery materials, EV battery separators and electrolytes, aluminum production, photovoltaic glass for solar panels and electric heavy-duty vehicles used in mining and other industries.

The first battery exports are being undertaken by REPT Battero Indonesia, one of the companies operating in the industrial complex.

"We will become an important part of the global electric vehicle battery supply chain," Rosan said during the ceremony, which was broadcast live on the government's YouTube channel.

IWIP has attracted approximately $20 billion in realized investment since beginning operations in 2018, with another $7 billion in investment commitments expected to bring the total to $27 billion, Rosan said.

The industrial park now hosts 52 companies from various countries and employs approximately 117,000 workers, making it one of Indonesia's major industrial centers outside Java.

Exports from IWIP have reached $11 billion, according to Rosan. Combined with exports from the Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP) in Central Sulawesi, which is also part of Indonesia's nickel-processing and battery supply chain, the two industrial complexes account for approximately $28 billion in exports.

Rosan said the combined figure was equivalent to around 10% of Indonesia's total exports.

Prabowo Sees Bright Future 

 Speaking at the inauguration ceremony, Prabowo described the first EV battery exports as evidence that Indonesia's downstream industrialization strategy was delivering results.

"Every month, there are predictions that we are going to collapse. But today, I came here and saw that Indonesia's future is bright," Prabowo said.

He said the development of Weda Bay and its industrial ecosystem demonstrated the country's ability to attract investment and build manufacturing capacity around its natural resources.

Prabowo also acknowledged the contribution of previous administrations, particularly that of former President Joko Widodo, who championed nickel industrialization and laid the groundwork for Indonesia's EV battery ecosystem.

"What we have witnessed today cannot be separated from what was done yesterday," Prabowo said.

title: Jakarta Stocks Slip Below 6,000 as Consumer Confidence Weakens
article:
Jakarta. Indonesian stocks reversed early gains to trade below the 6,000 level on Friday morning, fluctuating between 5,997 and 6,047 during the first trading session as investors weighed domestic economic indicators and weaker US technology stocks.

Jakarta Composite Index initially rose 0.13% to 6,039 before turning lower. Data from RTI showed 2.93 billion shares traded in the early minutes, with a transaction value of Rp 242.7 billion ($13.56 million) across 43,582 transactions. A total of 212 stocks advanced, 156 declined and 277 remained unchanged.

Phintraco Sekuritas said Indonesia’s Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) fell to 118.1 in September 2026 from 118.5 in August, which had marked a three-month high.

The decline was mainly driven by the Current Economic Conditions Index, which dropped to 107.5 from 109.4, its lowest level in 12 months.

“However, the Consumer Expectations Index rose to 128.7 from 127.6, supported by increases in the Income Expectations Index and the Job Availability Expectations Index,” Phintraco Sekuritas said.

Despite the dip in consumer confidence, vehicle sales showed continued growth in September.

Car sales in Indonesia rose 28.1% year-on-year (YoY) to 79,450 units in September, slowing from 32.4% growth in August. For the third quarter of 2026, car sales increased 21% YoY to 679,020 units.

Motorcycle sales climbed 15.37% YoY to 654,343 units in September, marking their highest level since October 2014 and the strongest growth since May 2026.

“As a result, motorcycle sales in Indonesia grew 3.71% YoY to 5.02 million units in the third quarter of 2026,” Phintraco Sekuritas added.

Meanwhile, US stocks closed lower for a second consecutive session on Thursday, with technology shares weighing on the broader market, Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia said.

The S&P 500 fell 0.47%, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.25%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.10%.

“Technology stocks were the main source of pressure after media reports indicated that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was lower than previously indicated,” Kiwoom said.

title: ‘Only Time Will Tell’: Indonesia on World Bank’s 5.2% Forecast
article:
Jakarta. The World Bank’s 5.2% forecast remains to be seen, according to a senior deputy minister, as Jakarta sets sights on more ambitious targets.

The World Bank has recently raised its 2026 outlook for Indonesia by 0.5 percentage points to 5.2% in 2026. The forecast for 2027 stays unchanged at 5.2%. Indonesia wants its economy to expand by 6% next year, the newly appointed Deputy Coordinating Economic Affairs Minister Dradjad Hari Wibowo announced Thursday.

Southeast Asia’s biggest economy expanded by 5.45% in the first half of 2026, and is aiming for a full-year growth of at least 5.4%. Asked about the World Bank’s forecasts, Dradjad only said that “only time will tell”, while saying that the government had already come up with plans to catapult growth.

“We have identified the sources of economic expansion. I’d say Q4 is a crucial time since its basis for growth is different. We have prepared steps to sustain growth this quarter,” Dradjad told the press on the margins of the Investor Daily Summit in Jakarta.

But Dradjad doesn’t want the economy to solely bank on stimulus packages, saying that it is also important to make sure that people are also self-reliant.

“Stimulus is not our only [strategy].”

Dradjad — who had only spent a week in the cabinet — signaled some “new initiatives” that will make businesses “extremely happy”, but stayed tight-lipped on the details. The senior economist hinted that these pleasant surprises could be in the form of regulatory improvements, while some would be aimed at “economic transformation”. The government has also allocated up to Rp 31 trillion ($1.7 billion) for a Q4 economic stimulus, with parts of the money going to cash subsidies and food aid.

On the 6% target, Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara said that the target would require a 7% year-on-year growth in investments. But this would not be a pipe dream, according to Suahasil, describing the state budget and the sovereign wealth fund Danantara as the country’s “two financial arms”.

“Sometimes we would use the state budget. Other times we would use Danantara. There are times when we would find a combination between public spending and Danantara’s investment to grow [the economy],” Suahasil told the same conference later that day.

The Prabowo Subianto administration aims to bring growth up to 8% by 2029.

title: TikTok’s Data Center Choice Exposes Indonesia’s High-Tech Talent Gap
article:
Jakarta.Indonesia’s lack of skilled workers is hampering efforts to attract high-tech investment, with TikTok choosing Thailand over Indonesia for a data center despite Indonesia being its largest market in Southeast Asia, a senior investment official said Thursday.

TikTok has more than 160 million users in Indonesia every month, compared with about 50 million in Thailand.

 

 “For TikTok, because the biggest market of TikTok in this region is Indonesia. But the data center of TikTok is in Thailand,” Nurul Ichwan, the Investment Ministry’s deputy for investment promotion, said at the Investor Daily Summit 2026 at Raffles Jakarta.

 

 “When we checked with them, what was the reason behind that you finally chose Thailand instead of Indonesia? They mentioned that we are not supported by sufficient enough manpower, talent that could support the operations of this data center,” he said.

Thailand’s Board of Investment approved $25 billion TikTok project in May to expand data infrastructure and data-processing capacity across Bangkok and neighboring provinces, reinforcing the country’s role as a regional digital hub.

The case highlights a broader challenge for Indonesia as it seeks to attract investment that brings technology, higher-value jobs and deeper integration into global supply chains, rather than simply more capital.

“It means that now the question in our homework is about how could we create the education center of having the graduations that will match with the technology operations,” Nurul said.

Indonesia is projected to need about 12 million digital workers by 2030, while the government estimates a shortfall of roughly 3 million. The Communications and Digital Ministry has set a target of producing 600,000 digital talents a year to narrow the gap. The shortage comes as competition for digital infrastructure investment intensifies across Southeast Asia.

He said Indonesia was mapping the technology required across its downstream programs to ensure the country could support more advanced production.

Nugraheni Utami, chief country representative of the US-ASEAN Business Council, said regulatory predictability was another key consideration for companies deciding where to invest and expand.

“Investment aftercare actually is really important, because we don't want an investor coming here, and they also have been struggling complying the regulation, especially when the regulation often change,” Utami said.

Indosat (ISAT) dan F5 Luncurkan Intelligence Suite, Sasar 50 Bisnis
article:
Penulis:Muhammad Alief Andri| Editor:Herlina Kartika Dewi

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) menggandeng perusahaan teknologi F5 untuk memperluas pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan atauartificial intelligence(AI) di Asia melalui peluncuran Indosat Intelligence Suite. Platform ini ditujukan untuk membantu perusahaan mengakses, mengelola, dan memperluas penggunaan AI dengan pengendalian biaya serta tata kelola yang terintegrasi.

Indosat menyebut Intelligence Suite mengintegrasikan lebih dari 300 model AI terbuka dan tertutup dalam satu antarmuka. Model yang tersedia mencakup Sahabat-AI, model yang dihosting oleh Indosat, serta berbagai model AI global.

Melalui platform ini, perusahaan dapat memilih model AI sesuai kebutuhan bisnis tanpa harus membangun dan mengelola sendiri seluruh infrastruktur yang mendasarinya. Sistem tersebut juga dirancang untuk membantu perusahaan mengarahkan permintaan ke model yang sesuai berdasarkan biaya, kualitas, dan latensi.

President Director and Chief Executive Officer Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison Vikram Sinha mengatakan, kebutuhan perusahaan terhadap AI kini tidak lagi terbatas pada akses ke model, tetapi juga mencakup kemampuan untuk menerapkannya secara aman dalam kegiatan operasional.

“Dengan berkembangnya AI dari tahap eksperimen ke penerapan dalam aktivitas bisnis sehari-hari, maka perusahaan pun membutuhkan lebih dari sekadar akses terhadap model AI. Mereka membutuhkan cara yang tepercaya untuk menerapkan kecerdasan ke dalam operasional bisnis,” ujar Vikram dalam keterangan resmi, Jumat (9/10/2026).

Ia menambahkan, Intelligence Suite dikembangkan dengan memanfaatkan ekosistem AI Indosat di Indonesia, yang mencakup energi, pusat data, komputasi, konektivitas, dan model AI.

“Denganfull-stackAI sebagai fondasi, Indosat Intelligence Suite akan menjadi intelligence factory, atau pabrik kecerdasan, bagi perusahaan, membantu mereka memilih AI yang tepat sesuai kebutuhan dan memperluas skalanya secara aman di seluruh kawasan,” katanya.

Kemitraan dengan F5 turut menghadirkan kemampuan pengelolaan dan perlindungan infrastruktur AI. Melalui F5 BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes, platform ini mendukung isolasi pengguna serta perlindungan lingkungan aplikasi berbasis kontainer. F5 juga menyediakan penyeimbangan beban kerja yang memperhitungkan kapasitas GPU untuk membantu mengoptimalkan latensi dan pemrosesan permintaan AI.

Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer F5 François Locoh-Donou mengatakan, kolaborasi ini bertujuan menghubungkan infrastruktur AI dengan kebutuhan perusahaan melalui sistem yang lebih terkelola.

“Indosat tengah membangun masa depan AI di kawasan, dan F5 bangga dapat membantu mengamankan dan mengoptimalkannya. Bersama-sama, kami membuat AI yang lebih canggih dapat diakses secara aman oleh setiap bisnis,” ujar François.

Dari sisi pengelolaan biaya, Intelligence Suite menawarkan mekanisme konversi token menjadi kredit yang dapat dialokasikan ke berbagai model, aplikasi, dan tim. Perusahaan juga dapat memilih skema layananPay as You Go, Unified Enterprise Credit, maupun Dedicated Capacity, sesuai kebutuhan dan skala penggunaan AI.

Platform ini turut menyediakan pengaturan keamanan dan tata kelola, termasuk autentikasi permintaan, pencatatan penggunaan yang dapat diaudit, serta pengaturan kebijakan untuk menentukan apakah beban kerja dapat diarahkan ke model global. Untuk organisasi yang memiliki persyaratan lokasi penyimpanan data, Sahabat-AI dan model yang dihosting Indosat dapat digunakan untuk memproses beban kerja di negara tempat organisasi tersebut beroperasi.

Chief Revenue Officer F5 Chad Whalen mengatakan, perusahaan masih menghadapi tantangan dalam membawa AI dari tahap uji coba ke penerapan produksi, terutama dalam menyeimbangkan inovasi dengan kedaulatan data, tata kelola, dan kepastian biaya.

Dengan menggabungkan jangkauan pasar Indosat dan teknologi keamanan F5, kedua perusahaan menargetkan platform tersebut dapat membantu bisnis menerapkan AI sesuai kebutuhan operasionalnya.

Saat diluncurkan, Indosat Intelligence Suite ditargetkan menjangkau 50 bisnis dan organisasi. Akses awal ditawarkan dengan harga promosi yang tersedia sepanjang tahun. Platform ini mulai tersedia pada Jumat (9/10/2026), melalui situs resminya untuk melihat katalog model, informasi harga, dokumentasi, dan mengajukan permintaan akses.

Peluncuran Intelligence Suite menjadi bagian dari strategi Indosat untuk memperluas pemanfaatan ekosistem AI yang telah dibangun di Indonesia ke kebutuhan bisnis yang lebih luas di kawasan Asia.

title: Danantara Buka Peluang Borong Saham Saat Pasar Tertekan
article:
Sumber:Reuters| Editor:Handoyo

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Badan pengelola investasi (sovereign wealth fund) Indonesia, Danantara, membuka peluang untuk menambah investasi di pasar saham domestik ketika terjadi tekanan pasar, sepanjang langkah tersebut dinilai menguntungkan secara investasi.

Di sisi lain, Danantara juga berhati-hati dalam menambah eksposur terhadap kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence/AI) dan tengah membahas kemungkinan menahan sebagian dividen yang seharusnya disetorkan kepada pemerintah.

Mengutip Reuters, Jumat (9/10/2026), strategi tersebut disampaikan sejumlah petinggi Danantara. Pernyataan itu memberikan gambaran lebih terperinci mengenai strategi investasi dan alokasi modal lembaga yang mengelola investasi publik, aset swasta, portofolio badan usaha milik negara (BUMN), hingga penjualan komoditas nasional tersebut.

Langkah Danantara juga menjadi perhatian investor di tengah kekhawatiran terhadap potensi tekanan lanjutan di pasar saham Indonesia.

Tekanan pasar berpotensi meningkat apabila penyedia indeks global MSCI menurunkan klasifikasi pasar Indonesia dalam pembaruan hasil peninjauannya bulan depan.Danantara Siapkan Investasi Tambahan

Head of public investment Danantara Investment Management, Rani Piputri, mengatakan pihaknya telah menginvestasikan sekitar US$ 3 miliar pada saham dan obligasi di pasar domestik maupun internasional.

Bergantung pada kondisi pasar, Danantara berencana mengalokasikan tambahan investasi sebesar US$ 1 miliar hingga akhir tahun ini.

Rani menjelaskan, Danantara dapat mempertimbangkan masuk ke pasar saham ketika terjadi gejolak yang dipicu sentimen eksternal bersifat sementara dan peluang investasinya dinilai menarik.

"Jika terjadi krisis di pasar dan kami menilai krisis tersebut hanya didasarkan pada sentimen eksternal yang bersifat sangat sementara, maka kami mungkin akan masuk ke pasar," ujar Rani kepada Reuters.

Menurut dia, Danantara telah melakukan pembelian saham secara bertahap sejak akhir tahun lalu hingga periode aksi jual besar-besaran yang menyusul peringatan MSCI pada Januari lalu.

Saat itu, MSCI memperingatkan kemungkinan menurunkan status pasar saham Indonesia dari kategori emerging market atau pasar negara berkembang menjadi frontier market atau pasar perbatasan.

Jika penurunan klasifikasi tersebut memicu aksi jual lanjutan pada bulan depan, Danantara tidak menutup kemungkinan kembali membeli saham di pasar domestik, selama langkah tersebut berpotensi menghasilkan keuntungan.

"Kami mungkin akan masuk. Mungkin saja, tetapi ada banyak uji tuntas yang harus kami lakukan," kata Rani.

Ia menegaskan, pembelian saham yang dilakukan Danantara sebelumnya didasarkan pada penilaian terhadap nilai investasi, bukan semata-mata untuk menopang atau menstabilkan pasar.

"Kami membeli saham pada awal tahun ini karena melihat adanya nilai investasi. Tujuannya bukan untuk menstabilkan pasar. Ada keuntungan ketika orang-orang tidak menyukai suatu aset, sementara kami melihat nilainya menarik, karena kami bisa mendapatkannya dengan harga yang bagus. Kemudian, ketika mereka kembali menyukainya, kami bisa menjualnya kepada mereka," jelasnya.

Pernyataan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa Danantara tetap menempatkan potensi imbal hasil sebagai pertimbangan utama dalam keputusan investasi, meskipun pembelian saham ketika pasar tertekan berpotensi memberikan sentimen positif bagi investor.Portofolio Danantara Didominasi Saham

Danantara diluncurkan pada awal 2025 dan bertanggung jawab langsung kepada Presiden Prabowo Subianto. Lembaga ini mendapat mandat mengelola aset negara senilai sekitar US$ 900 miliar yang tersebar di sekitar 1.000 perusahaan, sekaligus mengoptimalkan hasil investasi dari dividen perusahaan-perusahaan tersebut.

Rani, yang direkrut dari Wall Street untuk memimpin investasi publik Danantara, mengungkapkan bahwa sekitar 65% aset yang dikelola ditempatkan pada instrumen saham, 30% pada instrumen pendapatan tetap (fixed income), dan 5% pada dana lindung nilai (hedge fund).

Sekitar seperempat dari keseluruhan portofolio investasi tersebut dialokasikan ke Indonesia.

Selain pasar saham domestik, Danantara juga berinvestasi di pasar internasional untuk mendiversifikasi portofolio dan mencari peluang imbal hasil yang menarik.Danantara Berhati-hati Berinvestasi di Sektor AI

Di tengah meningkatnya perhatian investor global terhadap perkembangan teknologi kecerdasan buatan, Danantara memilih pendekatan yang terukur dalam meningkatkan eksposur terhadap sektor AI.

Rani menggambarkan strategi investasi Danantara di sektor tersebut sebagai langkah yang dilakukan secara cermat dan selektif.

"Kami tidak menganggap AI sebagai gelembung investasi dan tidak berpikir gelembung itu akan pecah. Namun, kami ingin berhati-hati saat mulai masuk ke sektor ini karena kami relatif terlambat," ujarnya.

Ia juga menilai munculnya diskusi mengenai potensi gelembung investasi AI dapat membantu menjaga kewaspadaan pelaku pasar.

"Anda mulai mendengar orang-orang membicarakan potensi gelembung investasi, dan itu bagus karena dapat menjaga pasar tetap terkendali. Jika semua orang menganggap AI sebagai investasi yang bagus, maka kami justru menghadapi masalah," kata Rani.

Sikap tersebut mencerminkan upaya Danantara untuk tetap memanfaatkan peluang pertumbuhan sektor teknologi, tanpa mengabaikan risiko valuasi dan potensi perubahan sentimen pasar.Danantara Targetkan Imbal Hasil di Atas Biaya Modal

Dalam wawancara terpisah, Direktur Pelaksana Hubungan Global dan Komunikasi Danantara Investment Management, Pahala Mansury, mengatakan Danantara menargetkan tingkat imbal hasil investasi sebesar 200 basis poin hingga 300 basis poin di atas biaya modalnya.

Sebagai acuan, biaya modal tersebut berada pada level 5,35%, berdasarkan penerbitan obligasi dolar AS bertenor lima tahun pada Juni lalu.

Dengan demikian, target imbal hasil Danantara berada sekitar 2 hingga 3 poin persentase di atas biaya modal tersebut. Jika menggunakan acuan 5,35%, kisaran targetnya setara dengan sekitar 7,35% hingga 8,35%.

Target tersebut menjadi salah satu tolok ukur bagi Danantara dalam mengelola aset negara dan menentukan alokasi investasi di berbagai instrumen keuangan.Dividen Rp 120 Triliun Masih Dibahas

Selain strategi investasi, Danantara juga tengah membahas rencana pembayaran dividen kepada pemerintah. Sebelumnya, mantan Menteri Keuangan Indonesia menyampaikan bahwa Danantara akan menyetorkan dividen sebesar Rp 120 triliun atau sekitar US$ 6,7 miliar kepada pemerintah pada tahun ini.

Namun, Pahala mengatakan dana dividen tersebut masih berpeluang dipertahankan untuk dikelola Danantara, bergantung pada hasil pembahasan dengan Menteri Keuangan yang baru, Suahasil Nazara.

"Kami sedang berdiskusi dengan Menteri Keuangan yang baru, Suahasil. Sejauh ini, indikasi yang kami terima adalah kami masih dapat mengelola dividen tersebut. Namun, tentu saja kami masih harus menunggu keputusan akhir," kata Pahala.

Jika dana tersebut tetap dikelola Danantara, keputusan itu berpotensi memberikan fleksibilitas tambahan dalam mengalokasikan modal untuk investasi. Meski demikian, kepastian mengenai penggunaan dividen tersebut masih menunggu keputusan pemerintah.

Pahala menegaskan bahwa Danantara tidak memiliki mandat eksplisit untuk menstabilkan pasar keuangan.

"Kami meyakini bahwa peran kami adalah memastikan apa pun yang kami lakukan tidak dipandang investor asing sebagai bentuk intervensi pasar, melainkan sebagai upaya untuk terus berkontribusi terhadap pendalaman pasar keuangan dan peningkatan tata kelola yang lebih baik," ujarnya.

title: Wall Street Naik Didorong Penurunan Harga Minyak Pasca Meredanya Kekhawatiran Pasokan
article:
Sumber:Reuters| Editor:Herlina Kartika Dewi

KONTAN.CO.ID -NEW YORK.Indeks utama Wall Street dibuka menguat pada awal perdagangan Jumat (9/10/2026), seiring turunnya Harga minyak akibat meredanya kekhawatiran pasokan di Timur Tengah. Meski saham telekomunikasi tetap berada di bawah tekanan setelah akuisisi spektrum oleh SpaceX memicu kekhawatiran persaingan di sektor tersebut.

Mengutip Reuters, pada bel pembukaan perdagangan indeks Dow Jones Industrial Average naik 67,32 poin, atau 0,13% ke level 51.298,96. S&P 500 naik 22,35 poin, atau 0,29%, menjadi 7.787,71, sementara Nasdaq Composite naik 149,59 poin, atau 0,55%, menjadi 27.342,93.

Harga minyak turun setelah Presiden AS Donald Trump mengatakan pada hari Kamis bahwa AS tidak akan menyerang Iran sebelum pemilihan paruh waktu AS bulan depan, sehingga meredakan kekhawatiran bahwa konflik tersebut dapat semakin mengganggu pasokan energi global.

Harga minyak mentah Brent turun lebih dari 1%, namun masih diperdagangkan di atas level psikologis US$ 100 per barel.

Imbal hasil (yield) obligasi pemerintah AS (Treasury) juga lebih stabil; imbal hasil acuan tenor 10 tahun bertahan di angka 5,24%, namun tetap berada di dekat level tertinggi dalam 24 tahun sebesar 5,364% yang dicapai pada hari Rabu.

Indeks acuan S&P 500 dan Nasdaq yang didominasi saham teknologi berada di jalur untuk mencatat kenaikan mingguan, meskipun sempat terkoreksi dalam dua sesi sebelumnya; sebelumnya, optimisme seputar musim laporan keuangan kuartal ketiga yang didorong oleh kecerdasan buatan (AI) telah mengangkat kedua indeks tersebut ke rekor tertinggi awal pekan ini.

Indeksblue-chipDow juga berada di jalur untuk mencatat kenaikan mingguan tipis, sementara indeks S&P 500 dengan bobot setara (equal-weighted) berpeluang mengakhiri tren penurunan selama tujuh minggu berturut-turut.

"Laporan keuangan yang kuat, panduan kinerja (guidance), dan bukti permintaan AI yang berkelanjutan dapat dengan cepat memulihkan keyakinan pasar dan kembali menempatkan potensi rekor tertinggi baru dalam jangkauan," ujar Chris Weston, kepala riset di Pepperstone.

Saham-saham pertumbuhan berkapitalisasi sangat besar (megacap) secara umum menguat pada hari itu; Nvidia naik 1,5% pada perdaganganpre market,Tesla naik 1,3%, sementara Amazon.com dan Alphabet mencatat kenaikan tipis.

Saham-saham sektor cip secara umum menguat sehari setelah sempat anjlok akibat laporan bahwa pendapatan tahunan OpenAI ternyata US$20 miliar lebih rendah dari angka yang sebelumnya diisyaratkan perusahaan. Sebuah ETF yang melacak kinerja produsen cip AS naik 1,6%.

Saham SpaceX naik 3,2% setelah perusahaan pembuat roket dan satelit tersebut mencapai kesepakatan untuk mengakuisisi portofolio spektrum pita rendah (low-band spectrum) berskala nasional, yang menjadi langkah awal tantangan langsung di orbit terhadap raksasa nirkabel lama di seluruh AS.

Saham perusahaan telekomunikasi diperdagangkan lebih rendah; saham T-Mobile US turun 7,2%, AT&T turun 6,9%, dan Verizon melemah 5,7%.

Musim laporan keuangan kuartalan akan semakin intensif pekan depan seiring dengan rencana bank-bank besar untuk merilis kinerja mereka. Optimisme mengenai kinerja keuangan yang kuat telah menopang saham-saham AS belakangan ini, meskipun terdapat perkembangan geopolitik yang tidak menentu dan kekhawatiran akan kenaikan suku bunga.

"Bank-bank ini menjadi indikator yang penting untuk dipahami: apakah masyarakat melakukan pinjaman, dan bagaimana situasi saat ini... hal itu juga akan memberikan data mengenai langkah apa yang mungkin atau tidak mungkin diambil oleh The Fed," ujar Kim Forrest, Chief Investment Officer di Bokeh Capital Partners.

title: Investasi Ditargetkan Rp 2.900 Triliun pada 2027, Ini Prospek Emiten Kawasan Industri
article:
Reporter:Pulina Nityakanti| Editor:Handoyo

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Emiten properti kawasan industri berpeluang mencatatkan pertumbuhan kinerja seiring ambisi pemerintah mendorong investasi nasional hingga Rp 2.900 triliun pada 2027. Meski demikian, prospek sektor ini akan bergantung pada realisasi investasi dan kemampuan pengelola kawasan mengonversi permintaan lahan menjadi pendapatan.

Pemerintah mengandalkan peningkatan investasi untuk mengejar target pertumbuhan ekonomi sebesar 6% pada 2027. Adapun realisasi investasi Indonesia pada semester I-2026 mencapai Rp 1.010,6 triliun, tumbuh 7,2% secara tahunan atau year on year (YoY).

Equity Research Analyst Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia Adrian Djie mengatakan, target investasi pemerintah tersebut berpotensi menjadi sentimen positif bagi kinerja emiten properti kawasan industri.

Menurut dia, kinerja emiten kawasan industri tercermin dari prapenjualan lahan yang umumnya mendahului realisasi investasi. Pertumbuhan realisasi investasi pada semester I-2026 juga menunjukkan bahwa minat investor masih terjaga.

“Sehingga, target investasi sebesar Rp 2.900 triliun pada 2027 mengindikasikan pipeline pembelian lahan baru yang berpotensi mengalir ke emiten kawasan industri,” ujarnya kepada Kontan, Jumat (9/10/2026).

Senior Market Analyst Mirae Asset Sekuritas Nafan Aji Gusta juga menilai target investasi tersebut berpotensi menjadi katalis positif bagi sektor properti kawasan industri.

Potensi dampaknya akan semakin besar apabila pertumbuhan investasi diikuti realisasi pembangunan pabrik, ekspansi kapasitas produksi, serta masuknya investasi baru di sektor manufaktur, kendaraan listrik (EV), baterai, pusat data atau data center, dan industri hilirisasi.

Namun, dampak positif tersebut diperkirakan tidak akan dirasakan secara merata oleh seluruh emiten.

“Perusahaan yang memiliki cadangan lahan siap jual, lokasi strategis, infrastruktur memadai, serta akses langsung terhadap kawasan industri yang menjadi tujuan investor berpeluang lebih cepat mengonversi pertumbuhan investasi menjadi penjualan lahan dan pendapatan berulang,” ujarnya kepada Kontan, Jumat (9/10).

Capaian investasi pada semester I-2026 menjadi salah satu indikasi positif bagi prospek sektor ini. Kendati demikian, pencapaian target investasi pada 2027 tetap bergantung pada realisasi proyek, bukan hanya komitmen atau pengumuman investasi.

Karena itu, investor perlu mencermati sejumlah indikator kinerja emiten kawasan industri, mulai dari pertumbuhan prapenjualan lahan industri, tingkat penyerapan lahan (land absorption), harga jual rata-rata lahan, hingga perkembangan proyek infrastruktur di sekitar kawasan.Kebijakan Sewa Lahan Jadi Sentimen Tambahan

Selain target investasi nasional, sentimen positif bagi sektor properti kawasan industri juga datang dari rencana pemerintah melalui Danantara untuk menghapus biaya sewa lahan di kawasan industri milik negara mulai 2027 guna menarik investor asing.

Kebijakan tersebut berpotensi meningkatkan daya tarik Indonesia sebagai tujuan investasi. Namun, di sisi lain, langkah ini juga dapat memperbesar persaingan bagi pengelola kawasan industri swasta.

“Dampak akhirnya akan bergantung pada apakah pertambahan investasi cukup besar untuk memperluas permintaan lahan secara keseluruhan,” paparnya.

Hingga 2027, prospek emiten properti kawasan industri dinilai masih moderat. Adrian berpandangan, salah satu pendorong utama kinerja sektor ini adalah relokasi pabrik dari negara lain yang mencari basis produksi di kawasan ASEAN.

Selain itu, pembangunan infrastruktur penunjang seperti jalan tol dan pelabuhan, serta permintaan lahan dari sektor hilirisasi dan pusat data, berpotensi mendukung pertumbuhan bisnis pengelola kawasan industri.

Meski begitu, terdapat sejumlah risiko yang perlu diperhatikan. Ketidakpastian tarif dan perdagangan global dapat mendorong investor menunda keputusan ekspansi. Pelemahan rupiah juga berpotensi meningkatkan biaya impor mesin dan bahan baku, sementara kondisi makroekonomi global dapat memengaruhi keputusan investasi perusahaan.

Sementara itu, Nafan melihat realisasi investasi manufaktur, ekspansi industri kendaraan listrik dan baterai, kebutuhan lahan untuk pusat data, serta relokasi fasilitas produksi ke Indonesia sebagai katalis utama sektor ini hingga 2027.

“Pembangunan infrastruktur dan konektivitas di kawasan industri baru dapat meningkatkan daya saing lokasi serta memperbesar peluang penjualan lahan,” katanya.

Di sisi lain, ketidakpastian ekonomi global, suku bunga yang masih relatif tinggi, pelemahan rupiah, biaya pembangunan infrastruktur, serta risiko penundaan realisasi investasi menjadi sejumlah sentimen pemberat bagi sektor tersebut.

Emiten kawasan industri juga perlu mengantisipasi perbedaan waktu antara pembelian lahan oleh investor dan pengakuan pendapatan dalam laporan keuangan. Kondisi ini membuat pertumbuhan penjualan lahan tidak selalu langsung tercermin dalam kinerja keuangan pada periode yang sama.

“Penilaian terhadap prospek sektor ini sebaiknya tidak hanya didasarkan pada target investasi pemerintah, tetapi juga pada kontrak penjualan lahan yang sudah terealisasi, kemampuan menghasilkan arus kas, dan struktur utang masing-masing emiten,” paparnya.Rekomendasi Saham SSIA

Di tengah prospek dan risiko tersebut, saham PT Surya Semesta Internusa Tbk (SSIA) menjadi salah satu pilihan yang direkomendasikan oleh analis.

Adrian merekomendasikantrading buyuntuk SSIA dengan target harga Rp 1.775 per saham. Sementara itu, Nafan merekomendasikan akumulasi beli SSIA dengan target harga Rp 2.010 per saham.

title: IKK September 2026 Turun Tipis, Ini Dampaknya bagi Emiten Konsumer
article:
Reporter:Rashif Usman| Editor:Handoyo

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Pelemahan keyakinan masyarakat terhadap kondisi ekonomi saat ini menjadi salah satu sinyal yang perlu dicermati investor di tengah tekanan terhadap saham sektor konsumer.

Meski indeks keyakinan konsumen (IKK) masih berada di zona optimistis, perubahan pola belanja masyarakat berpotensi memengaruhi penjualan dan margin keuntungan emiten.

Data Bank Indonesia menunjukkan IKK September 2026 tercatat sebesar 118,1, turun tipis dibandingkan 118,5 pada Agustus 2026.

Penurunan tersebut terutama dipengaruhi oleh melemahnya penilaian masyarakat terhadap kondisi ekonomi saat ini. Indeks kondisi ekonomi saat ini turun 1,9 poin menjadi 107,5, sekaligus menjadi level terendah dalam 12 bulan terakhir.

Persepsi konsumen terhadap ketersediaan lapangan kerja selama enam bulan terakhir juga melemah 3,0 poin menjadi 101,1. Sementara itu, ekspektasi terhadap kegiatan usaha turun 0,6 poin menjadi 121,5.

Head of Research Kiwoom Sekuritas Liza Camelia Suryanata mengatakan, pelemahan IKK menjadi sinyal peringatan dini bagi emiten, terutama karena persepsi masyarakat terhadap ketersediaan lapangan kerja ikut menurun. Kondisi tersebut dapat membuat konsumen lebih berhati-hati dalam membelanjakan uang ketika merasa keamanan penghasilannya berkurang.

Meski demikian, penurunan IKK dari 118,5 menjadi 118,1 masih relatif terbatas. Indeks tersebut juga tetap berada di atas level 100, sehingga belum cukup untuk menyimpulkan bahwa konsumsi masyarakat akan mengalami penurunan tajam.

Ekspektasi konsumen secara keseluruhan masih berada di zona optimistis, meskipun persepsi terhadap kondisi ekonomi saat ini semakin tertekan. Bagi emiten, perubahan perilaku belanja masyarakat menjadi hal yang perlu diantisipasi, mulai dari meningkatnya pencarian promosi, peralihan ke merek yang lebih murah, hingga pengurangan jumlah barang yang dibeli.

"Penjualan bisa tetap jalan, tapi untungnya makin tipis. Peluang tetap ada untuk produk kebutuhan sehari-hari dengan harga terjangkau, ditambah momentum belanja Natal & akhir tahun," kata Liza kepada Kontan, Jumat (9/10/2026).

Secara terpisah, Analis Mega Capital Sekuritas Revo Gilang Firdaus menilai penurunan IKK sebesar 0,4 poin menjadi sinyal adanya perlambatan kondisi konsumsi domestik.

Namun, menurut Revo, pelemahan tersebut tidak serta-merta menunjukkan bahwa kondisi ekonomi Indonesia sedang lemah. Pasalnya, IKK masih berada di atas 100 yang mengindikasikan bahwa konsumen masih berada dalam zona optimistis.

Revo mengatakan, saham-saham sektor konsumer memang cenderung mengalami tekanan sejak awal tahun di tengah perkembangan sentimen global. Selain itu, perhatian investor juga tertuju pada sektor lain sehingga tekanan terhadap saham konsumer semakin besar.

"Saran bagi investor adalah bisa mempertimbangkan tactical trading mengikuti story yang berkembang saat ini apabila menjadi seorang trader," jelas Revo.Saham Ritel dan Kebutuhan Pokok Memiliki Tingkat Sensitivitas Berbeda

Liza menilai, emiten seperti ERAA dan MAPI relatif lebih sensitif terhadap pelemahan daya beli masyarakat. Konsumen berpotensi menunda pembelian gadget, pakaian, maupun produk gaya hidup ketika kondisi keuangan dirasakan semakin terbatas.

Meski demikian, peluncuran produk baru dan kekuatan merek masih dapat menjadi faktor yang menarik minat pembeli.

Sebaliknya, emiten seperti ICBP, INDF, dan AMRT dinilai relatif lebih tahan terhadap perubahan pola konsumsi. Masyarakat tetap membutuhkan makanan dan barang kebutuhan sehari-hari, meskipun jumlah produk yang dibeli atau nilai belanjanya berpotensi berkurang.

"Jadi emiten kebutuhan pokok pun tetap harus diperhatikan marginnya, apalagi kalau biaya naik sementara menaikkan harga jual makin sulit," ucap Liza.

Bagi investor, Liza menyarankan agar mencermati laporan keuangan emiten pada periode berikutnya. Beberapa indikator yang perlu diperhatikan meliputi pertumbuhan volume penjualan, penjualan gerai yang sama atausame-store sales, serta besarnya diskon yang diberikan perusahaan untuk mendorong pertumbuhan penjualan.

"Saya lebih suka emiten yang tetap bisa jualan dan menjaga keuntungan, dengan valuasi masuk akal. Jangan membeli hanya karena merasa konsumer pasti aman," tambah Liza.Cukai MBDK Berpotensi Menekan Margin Emiten Konsumer

Selain pelemahan keyakinan konsumen, rencana penerapan cukai minuman berpemanis dalam kemasan (MBDK) yang direncanakan mulai berlaku pada semester II-2027 menjadi salah satu sentimen yang perlu diperhatikan investor.

Revo mengatakan, kebijakan tersebut berpotensi meningkatkan beban biaya bagi produsen minuman berpemanis. Dampaknya terhadap masing-masing emiten akan bergantung pada komposisi produk dan seberapa besar kegiatan usahanya terpapar kebijakan tersebut.

Besarnya kontribusi pendapatan dari segmen minuman tidak serta-merta mencerminkan tingkat eksposur perusahaan terhadap cukai MBDK. Pasalnya, tidak semua produk minuman otomatis masuk dalam cakupan kebijakan tersebut.

Investor karena itu perlu mencermati potensi tekanan terhadap margin keuntungan dan permintaan. Risiko tersebut dapat meningkat apabila produsen tidak mampu meneruskan seluruh tambahan beban cukai kepada konsumen melalui kenaikan harga jual.

Dalam kondisi konsumsi yang berpotensi melambat, kemampuan perusahaan menjaga daya saing harga sekaligus mempertahankan profitabilitas menjadi salah satu faktor penting dalam menilai kinerja emiten konsumer.

"Investor dapat mencermati emiten konsumer yang basis fundamental sudah sangat kuat diikuti dengan produk yang relatif defensif dan dibutuhkan di tengah kondisi ekonomi saat ini," tutur Revo.

title: Pefindo Pangkas Peringkat Danareksa, Imbas Perannya Jadi Holding Kawasan Industri
article:
Reporter:Avanty Nurdiana| Editor:Avanty Nurdiana

KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA.PT Pemeringkat Efek Indonesia (Pefindo) menurunkan peringkat PT Danareksa beserta obligasi yang masih beredar dari idAA menjadi idA+. Penurunan peringkat ini sejalan dengan perubahan peran Danareksa dari holding lintas sektor menjadi holding yang berfokus pada pengelolaan kawasan industri.

Pefindo dalam riset pada 8 Oktober 2026 menjelaskan, penetapan peringkat idA+ ini berlaku untuk General Obligation (GO), Obligasi VII, dan Obligasi VIII Danareksa. Peringkat tersebut berlaku untuk periode 6 Oktober 2026 hingga 1 Oktober 2027, dengan prospek atau outlook stabil.

Pefindo menjelaskan, penurunan peringkat tersebut terutama mencerminkan berkurangnya kemungkinan dukungan pemerintah kepada Danareksa seiring transformasi bisnis perusahaan.

Sebelumnya, Danareksa merupakan holding yang mencakup berbagai sektor, termasuk jasa keuangan, konstruksi, dan kawasan industri. Kini, perusahaan berfokus menjadi holding khusus kawasan industri.

Perubahan tersebut memengaruhi penilaian Pefindo terhadap kemungkinan pemerintah memberikan dukungan luar biasa kepada Danareksa ketika perusahaan menghadapi tekanan keuangan, termasuk dengan mempertimbangkan peran strategis perusahaan, dampak sosial, serta konsekuensi jika terjadi gagal bayar.

Meski peringkatnya turun, Pefindo menilai Danareksa masih memiliki kemungkinan dukungan pemerintah yang cukup tinggi. Perusahaan juga dinilai memiliki posisi yang kuat di industri kawasan industri serta fleksibilitas keuangan yang kuat.

Namun, peringkat Danareksa masih dibatasi oleh struktur permodalan, perlindungan arus kas yang moderat, serta paparan terhadap kondisi makroekonomi yang kurang menguntungkan.

Sebagai holding kawasan industri BUMN, Danareksa mengelola tujuh kawasan industri di Indonesia. Portofolionya mencakup PT Kawasan Industri Medan, PT Kawasan Industri Wijayakusuma, PT Kawasan Industri Makassar, PT Kawasan Berikat Nusantara, PT Surabaya Industrial Estate Rungkut, PT Kawasan Industri Terpadu Batang, dan PT Jakarta Industrial Estate Pulogadung.

Dalam penilaian Pefindo, prospek peringkat Danareksa dapat membaik apabila perusahaan mampu memperkuat posisi pasar melalui perluasan portofolio kawasan industri yang dikelola, disertai perbaikan rasio leverage keuangan.

Sebaliknya, peringkat berpotensi kembali turun apabila Danareksa gagal mencapai target pendapatan atau profitabilitas. Risiko penurunan juga dapat muncul apabila belanja modal dibiayai dengan tambahan utang yang melampaui proyeksi tanpa didukung prospek bisnis yang kuat, atau jika peran dan kontribusi perusahaan bagi pemerintah berkurang ketika menghadapi tekanan keuangan.

Dari sisi keuangan, Danareksa membukukan penjualan sebesar Rp1,85 triliun per Juni 2026. Sementara itu, EBITDA tercatat Rp 654,2 miliar dan laba bersih setelah kepentingan nonpengendali mencapai Rp 1,003 triliun.

Margin EBITDA Danareksa pada Juni 2026 tercatat 35,3%, lebih rendah dibandingkan 39,5% pada akhir 2025 dan 43,5% pada akhir 2024.

Dari sisi neraca, total aset yang disesuaikan mencapai Rp 63,57 triliun per Juni 2026. Adapun total utang yang disesuaikan sebesar Rp 4,64 triliun, dengan total ekuitas yang disesuaikan mencapai Rp 40,29 triliun.

Rasio utang disesuaikan terhadap ekuitas disesuaikan tercatat sebesar 0,1 kali pada Juni 2026, relatif sama dengan posisi akhir 2025, tetapi lebih rendah dibandingkan 0,3 kali pada akhir 2024.

Meski demikian, Pefindo menilai struktur permodalan dan perlindungan arus kas masih menjadi faktor pembatas peringkat Danareksa. Dengan prospek stabil, peringkat saat ini mencerminkan ekspektasi bahwa profil kredit perusahaan akan tetap terjaga, dengan tetap memperhatikan perkembangan bisnis dan dukungan pemerintah.
